why: Paragraphs. Every line used to search to the end of the file for a line ending the file does not use.
Blank lines, for the same reason, with nothing else to hide it.
Lines ended by a carriage return alone, which is the same search for the other character.
Lines ended by both characters.
A flat list.
A list that changes its marker at every item, so every item opens a new list.
A quotation carried on by lazy lines.
Setext headings.
One setext heading of many lines. A Dart string copies itself to be added to.
One paragraph of many lines, for the same reason.
Headings that are all different.
Headings that are all the same, each of which has to find a name nobody has.
HTML blocks.
A fence that is never closed.
Many fences.
A definition list.
A table with many rows.
A table with many columns.
A table cell of escaped pipes, built a character at a time.
A table after a long paragraph.
Link definitions that are all different.
Link definitions that are all the same.
Link definitions between lines of text.
A link label past the length a label may have. The regular expression must not run out of room on it.
A long title in a link definition.
Footnote definitions.
A footnote with a long indented body, taken a line at a time rather than spread into a call.
Footnote references that all resolve.
Brackets that never close.
Brackets nested as deep as they are long. Every `]` used to fold everything back to its opener.
Open brackets and then links, each of which turns off the brackets under it.
Footnote references that never close.
Footnote references that all close at the same far bracket.
Links in bold, a paragraph of which has a delimiter left for every one of them.
One link around a great deal of emphasis.
Links inside links.
Images inside images.
Destinations in angle brackets that never close. Each one used to read to the end of the text.
Titles in brackets that never close, for the same reason.
Reference labels that never close.
One reference label past the length a label may have.
Runs of backticks that are all different lengths, none of which closes.
Code spans.
Angle brackets. Dart used to copy the rest of the text at every one.
Tags that never close.
Attributes that never close.
A tag with a great many attributes.
A comment that never closes.
Inline HTML that does close.
Autolinks that never close.
Bare addresses, each of which used to copy the text after it in Dart, and to go on the stack here.
An address ending in closing brackets, which were counted again for each one.
Something that keeps nearly being an e-mail address.
Hard breaks of two spaces.
Hard breaks of a backslash.
Emphasis that never closes.
Underscores either side of a word.
Two kinds of emphasis, neither of which closes.
Inline directives whose labels never close, read to the end of the line from every colon.
Inline directives inside each other, which ran out of stack at twenty-four kilobytes.
Container directives inside each other.
Quotation markers on one line.
List markers on one line.
A long run of letters with nothing to stop on.
Character references.
